summary: Thamra is an AI-integrated decision support tool created by Bahraini youths that helps farmers adapt to changes in their environment. It uses data from NASA earth observation satellites, Sentinel-2 and information on agricultural suitability from the FAO-IIASA to provide farmers with an easy to understand insight into the environment. With features such as AI assistance, adaptive field analysis, early disease detection and intelligent crop rotation suggestions, Thamra provides farmers with an interactive map of their farm, environmental monitoring, crop compatibility and crop rotation tools. This allows farmers to look into different crop options. The tool was designed to help with issues facing the agricultural industry including water shortages, increased temperatures and salinization of the soils. Thamra will help to promote sustainable and efficient farming practices. In the future we hope to utilize AI, satellite technology and local knowledge to help farmers make better decisions
details:
Thamra is an AI-integrated agricultural decision-support platform developed by Bahraini youth to help local farmers make more informed decisions and adapt to changing environmental conditions. Designed with Bahrain's agricultural challenges in mind, Thamra addresses water scarcity, rising temperatures and soil salinity through a combination of Earth observation, agricultural data and artificial intelligence.

The platform brings together multiple data sources, including NASA POWER climate observations, NASA GPM precipitation estimates, Sentinel-2 satellite imagery and FAO–IIASA GAEZ crop suitability information. These datasets help build environmental profiles, assess vegetation conditions and evaluate potential crop suitability. Using this information, Thamra generates exploratory crop rotation recommendations, allowing farmers to compare crop combinations and understand the environmental factors behind them.

Thamra's farmer-facing interface includes an interactive satellite farm map, environmental monitoring, crop rotation planning, crop compatibility analysis and an AI-powered assistant that makes agricultural information more accessible. The platform also incorporates early plant disease recognition as part of its AI-assisted capabilities.

The project was developed using Python, Pandas and NumPy for data processing and analysis, Google Colab for notebook execution, Google Earth Engine for GPM data processing, and Microsoft Planetary Computer for accessing Sentinel-2 imagery. The interface uses HTML, CSS and JavaScript.

Thamra's creativity lies in connecting global Earth observation data with Bahrain's local agricultural context through an accessible, AI-integrated experience. Our team considered environmental conditions, water availability, crop diversity, agricultural suitability and the importance of local farming knowledge.

Our intended impact is to encourage climate-adaptive agriculture, improve resource awareness and support more resilient farming decisions. Thamra aims to empower farmers with accessible insights while complementing, rather than replacing, their experience and judgement.
